description: Issue #570: make active Agent work recoverable across Runner OOM/restart — recoverable interruption records with bounded terminal fallback, durable Runner work journal with factual reconciliation, runtime-independent control plane with per-runtime claim gating, bounded quarantine/teardown, per-work resource isolation, and user-visible recovery states replacing terminal runner-lost.

tasks.title: Workflow interruption record, closeout semantics, and bounded recovery fallback (server)
tasks.description: Replace the terminal `FailActiveWorkAsync(workerId, "runner-lost")` in `RunnerGrain.CloseoutLostAsync` with an identity-fenced `MarkWorkInterruptedAsync(workerId, reasonCode, interruptedAt, recoveryDeadline)` that records an at-most-one `WorkflowRun.WorkInterruption` (workKey, workId/taskRunId/isChecks, reasonCode `runner-lost`|`runner-unregistered`, recoveryDeadlineAt = interruptedAt + `RunnerRecoveryTimeout`, default 15 min) committed transactionally with events via `SaveAsync(run, events)`. Settlement-fenced Agent tasks keep their #589 unknown settlement (closeout keeps calling `ObserveAgentRunnerDisconnectedAsync` first; the interruption record is written only when no settlement fences the work); the dispatch snapshot is retained for interrupted work. Arm a `runner-recovery` Orleans reminder from the persisted absolute deadline (idempotent ensure-on-activation, re-register on tick-before-deadline, unregister after state commit) that on expiry with no Runner having accepted or reported fires exactly one terminal transition (`TaskFailed`/checks failure with reason `runner-lost-recovery-expired`) followed by snapshot deletion and lock release.
acceptanceCriteria: Presence-timeout closeout of an ordinary task or stage checks run records a WorkInterruption with reason code and recovery deadline, keeps run status Running, and writes no TaskFailed/completion from the closeout itself (SpecTests: presence timeout with ordinary task running).

Closeout of a workflow Agent task with an unresolved #589 settlement preserves the unknown settlement, disconnect reason, and settlement deadline, and writes no interruption record — a task has at most one fence, pinned by a test covering both closeout branches.
Deliberate unregister uses reason `runner-unregistered`; both reason codes are stable strings shared with status surfaces.
The dispatch snapshot for interrupted work is retained (still desired for redelivery) and deleted only at terminal fallback or report acceptance.
Recovery before the deadline (Runner reports/accepts) resolves the interruption with no terminal fallback applied (SpecTests with injected TimeProvider: runner returns before the deadline).

Deadline expiry with no Runner acceptance/report produces exactly one terminal transition naming `runner-lost-recovery-expired`, deletes the snapshot, and releases the stage lock; reminder re-registration/unregistration is idempotent (SpecTests with fake time and reminder entry points).
Re-closeout (idempotent repeated closeout calls) does not create a second interruption record or a second terminal transition.
`npm run test:fast:unit` and the SpecTests suite for workflow closeout/recovery pass.
No code path in WorkflowGrain/RunnerGrain terminal-fails active workflow work as `runner-lost` anymore.
tasks.output: Server changes: WorkflowRun domain (WorkInterruption record), IWorkflowGrain/WorkflowGrain interruption marking + runner-recovery reminder + terminal fallback, RunnerGrain.CloseoutLostAsync closeout branch, RunnerRecoveryTimeout configuration; SpecTests coverage for closeout, settlement-fence branch, recovery-before-deadline, expiry, and idempotency.
tasks.notes: Design Decisions A and E (workflow side). Do not reuse AgentResultSettlement for ordinary tasks — it suppresses redelivery, ordinary work needs the opposite. Do not redesign #589 settlement or #562 stop protocols; consume them. Migration plan step 1.

tasks.title: AgentJob recovery ledger state, reclaim under original identity, and recovery-expiry terminal (server)
tasks.description: Extend `AgentJobState` with interruption fields (`InterruptionReasonCode`, `InterruptedAt`, `RecoveryDeadlineAt`, set only while Status == Running) stamped by presence-loss closeout on every running ledger assigned to the lost Runner. Status projections (`GetRuntimeSnapshotAsync`, read models) derive a `Recovering` state whenever the fields are present and the deadline is unexpired — never silently `Running`. The recovery deadline rides the existing `CheckTimeoutsAsync`/reminder machinery: on expiry with no Runner having accepted or reported, the job enters exactly one terminal state with `FailureReason = runner-lost-recovery-expired`. A recovering AgentJob becomes claimable again by any eligible Runner under the original `JobKey`/`WorkId`/`DispatchJson` — no replacement work id or ledger row — with claim arbitration on the existing revision/claim fencing so if the original Runner also returns exactly one claim wins.
acceptanceCriteria: Closeout of a lost Runner stamps interruption fields on its running AgentJob ledgers, and `GetRuntimeSnapshotAsync`/read models project `Recovering` with the recorded reason while the deadline is unexpired (SpecTests: AgentJob running on the lost Runner).

A recovering AgentJob is re-admitted for assignment and claimed under its original work id and ledger row; claim/revision fencing admits exactly one claim when two Runners race, and the loser's reports are acknowledged stale (SpecTests: recoverable-interrupted AgentJob is reclaimed).
Report acceptance or Runner acceptance of a recovering job clears the interruption fields and returns the projection to a running/terminal path without a new work id.

Deadline expiry (injected TimeProvider) yields exactly one terminal transition with `runner-lost-recovery-expired` naming the interruption, no invented success, and no second terminal transition afterwards.
AgentJob report arbitration keeps runner/work identity match plus recovering-state eligibility; stale reports cannot overwrite an authoritative result.
SpecTests/UnitTests for closeout stamping, recovering projection, reclaim fencing, and expiry pass under `npm run test:fast:unit`.
tasks.output: Server changes: AgentJobState interruption fields, AgentJobGrain closeout stamping + Recovering projection + reclaim re-admission + recovery-expiry terminal in timeout reconciliation; SpecTests coverage.
tasks.notes: Design Decision B. Builds on the closeout restructure from T-001 (same CloseoutLostAsync branch). Rejected alternative (leave Running and rely on job timeout → Unknown) must not resurface. Migration plan step 2.

tasks.title: Identity-preserving redelivery and idempotent late-report reconciliation (server)
tasks.description: Keep interrupted workflow work desired for redelivery: `RenderActiveWorkflowAsync` keeps returning the stored snapshot while the interruption record exists, so a reconnected Runner that does not hold the work receives the original dispatch (same `ownerKind:ownerId:workId`, same payload, same report key); a Runner that still holds it skips re-execution via the existing held-key check. Extend #589's report arbitration (`FindReportableTaskAttempt`/`FindReportableWork` in WorkflowReportService/WorkflowGrain.Reports) so a report for recoverable-interrupted work is accepted at most once and resolves the interruption, and a report after settle/reassignment is acknowledged `Stale`. Make `missing-workflow` and `not-running` explicit members of the stale-ack family — terminal for Runner retry purposes with no owner state change — so the report path never returns an untracked dead end for preserved identities. AgentJob reports keep runner/work identity match plus recovering-state eligibility.
acceptanceCriteria: A reconnected Runner without the work receives the original dispatch (identical work identity and payload, no second task attempt); a Runner that holds the key receives it again and the redelivery is a no-op server-side (SpecTests: same Runner reconnects and still holds the work; restarted Runner receives redelivery).

A late report arriving while the work is still recoverable-interrupted and unsettled is accepted at most once under the preserved identity, resolves the interruption, and the ack retires the Runner's awaiting-ack entry (SpecTests).

A report arriving after the outcome was authoritatively recorded (settled, reassigned, or terminal-fallback applied) is acknowledged stale, the recorded outcome is unchanged, and no duplicate result event or second terminal transition appears in task history (SpecTests: late result after settle/reassign; duplicate report delivery).

`missing-workflow`/`not-running` acknowledgements are explicit stale-family terminal acks: the reporting Runner retires its awaiting-ack entry and no retry loop spins forever; no 404/untracked dead end for a preserved identity.
No work executes twice as a result of loss and recovery in the SpecTests reconnect/redelivery scenarios.
Full SpecTests for redelivery and report reconciliation pass under `npm run test:fast:unit`.
tasks.output: Server changes: DispatchService/RenderActiveWorkflowAsync snapshot retention for interrupted work, WorkflowReportService + WorkflowGrain.Reports arbitration extension (at-most-once accept + stale family incl. missing-workflow/not-running), AgentJob report arbitration for recovering identities; SpecTests coverage.
tasks.notes: Design Decision D. Wire protocol shape is unchanged — only semantics. Terminal tasks fence duplicates so task history cannot gain a second terminal transition. Migration plan steps 1–2 (server redelivery/report slice).

tasks.title: Durable Runner work journal and restart reconciliation
tasks.description: Add a `WorkJournal` store in `.mohist/runner-state/` patterned on `TerminalTaskLogDeliveryStoreImpl` (atomic text writes, serialized write chain, load-on-start, ready() gate), one entry per work key: `{workKey, dispatch, phase executing|awaitingAck, result?, binding?, startedAt, attempts, retryAt?}`. The in-memory in-flight/awaiting-ack maps in `RunnerHost` remain live state with the journal as their durable shadow, written only on transitions (accept / result produced / ack → delete). On process start the host loads the journal before its first poll and re-declares surviving keys: awaitingAck entries reload into the map and `retryDueReports()` re-reports the recorded result under the original report key; executing entries enter a recovering bucket that the reconciliation loop re-drives through `executeAndTransition` under the original key — recorded verdict facts (journal result, terminal task-log record) are reported rather than re-executed, a runtime binding whose session survived the restart is re-attached and the turn resumed, otherwise the work re-executes from the original dispatch under the original identity. No outcome is synthesized for an execution whose verdict is unknown — that surfaces through the existing unknown observation path.
acceptanceCriteria: Journal writes happen only on the three transitions (accept, result, ack-delete) and are atomic; the journal is bounded by the slot count.

After a simulated process restart (host torn down and reconstructed against the same runner-state directory, in the style of `execution-envelope.startup.test.ts`), the first poll report declares every surviving work key, so the server reconciles against facts instead of treating the works as unclaimed (runner vitest: restart after kill with works in flight and awaiting ack).

A work whose verdict was already journalled (or has a persisted terminal task-log record) is reported from the recorded facts and never re-executed; the owner observes at most one outcome for that identity (runner vitest).

An executing entry whose runtime binding session survived the restart is re-attached (turn resumed) instead of re-executed; a binding-less or dead-session entry re-executes under the original dispatch and work key with the held-key skip preventing duplicate execution on redelivery (runner vitest with fake runtime sessions).
Redelivery of a key the restarted Runner already holds (in-flight or awaiting-ack) is skipped with no duplicate execution.

Journal store unit tests cover atomicity, load-on-start with a ready() gate, corrupted/partial-entry tolerance, and deletion semantics; tests use the file-system seam and `vi.useFakeTimers` per project convention.
`npm test -w packages/runner` (typecheck + vitest) passes.
tasks.output: Runner changes: WorkJournal store + tests, RunnerHost wiring (shadow writes on transitions, load-on-start before first poll, first-poll declaration, recovering-bucket re-drive via executeAndTransition, verdict/runtime-binding reconciliation); restart/held-work/redelivery tests.
tasks.notes: Design Decision C. JSON-store pattern (not SQLite) — proven, tested, consistent with other runner-state stores. Rejected alternatives: empty-first-poll server redelivery alone (loses awaiting-ack verdicts) and embedded DB. Migration plan step 3. Note: server-side acceptance from T-003 is what makes the declared facts reconcile cleanly.

tasks.title: Runtime-independent control plane with per-runtime claim gating and deferred work
tasks.description: Restructure the `RunnerHost` readiness gate: the poll loop, heartbeat, SignalR connection, and awaiting-ack report retries run unconditionally for the life of the process; the only remaining admission gates are the local durability gates (task-log delivery store, runtime-event outbox) — a runtime failure alone never pauses polling. The poll request gains per-runtime readiness flags (`readyRuntimes: ["opencode", "pi"]` derived from each runtime's ready()/diagnostic), and `DispatchService` filters claim candidates whose required runtime is not reported ready so the work stays claimable by other Runners. Work the Runner already holds whose runtime is unavailable defers: the key stays in the reported set (occupying its slot) with identity/payload/report key preserved, no result report is emitted, and the runtime's actionable diagnostic (`server-spawn-failed`/`health-failed`/`server-exit` + recovery suggestion) is surfaced as an execution observation — never a synthesized failure; when the runtime recovers the deferred work executes under its original key. The heartbeat endpoint additionally refreshes presence (`TouchPresenceAsync`) so control-plane liveness has two independent proofs.
acceptanceCriteria: While OpenCode is quarantined/rebuilding with other work in flight, the Runner keeps polling, heartbeating, and retrying awaiting-ack reports, and server-side presence does not time out solely from OpenCode unhealthiness (runner vitest with fake runtimes + server DispatchService tests).

While Pi is unavailable and OpenCode healthy, the Runner claims and executes OpenCode-bound and runtime-independent work; only Pi-bound claiming is gated (runner vitest + DispatchService claim-filtering tests for the readyRuntimes body, including absence-of-field back-compat = today's behavior).

Held work requiring an unavailable runtime defers: identity, dispatch payload, and report key preserved; no failure/success report emitted while deferred; the slot stays occupied in the poll report; on runtime recovery it executes under the original identity and the owner observes at most one outcome (runner vitest).

The runtime diagnostic identifying the failing runtime and failure stage is emitted as an execution observation with a recovery suggestion and is never presented as a failure of the deferred work or a whole-Runner stop.
Interruption with no durable verdict never replays or synthesizes an outcome — it surfaces as an observation with a reason (pinned by a runner vitest case).
Heartbeat route calls `TouchPresenceAsync` so presence survives even if polls stall (server UnitTests/SpecTests).
`npm test -w packages/runner` and `npm run test:fast:unit` pass.
tasks.output: Runner changes: RunnerHost poll/heartbeat/report-loop unconditioning, readyRuntimes flag production, held-work deferral with observation-only diagnostics; Server changes: DispatchService per-runtime claim filtering, heartbeat presence refresh; tests on both sides.
tasks.notes: Design Decision F. Server-side claim filtering is the primary mechanism (a Runner with a dead runtime must not claim runtime-bound work and starve healthy Runners); local deferral remains for already-held work, which cannot be handed back without losing identity. New wire fields are additive; release is coordinated Server→Runner per the no-rolling-compat policy. Migration plan step 4 (liveness half).

tasks.title: Bounded quarantine drain, process-tree termination, and transport teardown
tasks.description: Give `RuntimeGeneration` an injectable quarantine drain deadline (`deps.quarantineDrainDeadlineMs`, driven by the existing `RuntimeClock` seam, default 60s): arming quarantine with active turns arms the timer; expiry resolves `generation.drained`, marks the generation force-destroyed, terminates the OpenCode server process tree and destroys transports, and normalizes still-unresolved turns to interrupted execution observations (reason `runtime-quarantine-destroyed`) through the existing `normalizeInterrupted` path — an observation, never a synthesized result — so the replacement generation build proceeds within the bound. Make `server-process.ts` `terminateTree` bounded: graceful close raced against a timeout, on expiry the undici dispatcher is destroyed rather than awaited; process-tree termination escalates SIGTERM → bounded grace → SIGKILL using the escalation pattern in `system/process.ts`, force-killing the server pid directly where the SDK exposes it. Route all runtime shutdown paths (OpenCode, Pi, runner shutdown) through these bounded helpers.
acceptanceCriteria: A generation quarantined with a turn that never settles is destroyed within the drain deadline (process tree terminated, transports destroyed), the replacement generation build proceeds, and the runtime returns to ready or explicitly-failed within the bound (runner vitest with RuntimeClock seam).
A generation whose active turns settle before the deadline is released and replaced without forced destruction (orderly-drain scenario).
Turns unresolved at force-destroy become interrupted execution observations with reason `runtime-quarantine-destroyed`, never result reports (never a synthesized outcome).
Dispatcher close with a hung in-flight request completes within its bound by destroying the dispatcher; the rebuild/shutdown path does not hang (runner vitest with a fake hung request).

A server process tree ignoring graceful termination is force-killed within the bounded grace period, and shutdown/replacement completes without waiting on the wedged tree; escalation SIGTERM→SIGKILL is covered by unit tests on the bounded helpers.

All runtime shutdown paths (OpenCode server-process, Pi runtime, runner shutdown) route through the bounded helpers — grep/code review confirms no unbounded `await dispatcher.close()`/tree-terminate remains.
Verify whether the pinned OpenCode SDK exposes the server child pid for direct SIGKILL escalation; use it when available, otherwise rely on scoped unit kill (open question in design).
`npm test -w packages/runner` passes.
tasks.output: Runner changes: RuntimeGeneration quarantine drain deadline + force-destroy path, bounded terminateTree with dispatcher destroy, bounded escalation in system/process.ts, bounded Pi/OpenCode/runner shutdown routing; vitest coverage via RuntimeClock and fake timers.
tasks.notes: Design Decision G. Complements (not replaces) resource isolation: the cgroup reclaims memory runaways, the deadline bounds logically hung turns/requests. Migration plan step 4 (teardown half).

tasks.title: Per-work resource isolation: launcher seam, containment reporting, and deployment assets
tasks.description: Introduce a `WorkExecutionLauncher` seam that launches each work item's action/child process tree under a per-work transient scope (`systemd-run --scope`, unit named from the sanitized work key, `MemoryMax`/`TasksMax` from deployment config) with an in-process fallback for non-systemd platforms where isolation is advisory and Decision G's deadlines remain the correctness guarantee. Kernel reclamation of a work scope is observed by the Runner as child death: it escalates containment (bounded kill of survivors via the T-006 helpers), frees the slot, and reports a terminal result with reason `resource-contained` — a factual verdict, not `runner-lost` and not a silent loss; shared runtime servers run under `mohist-runtime.slice` and never die with one work item, and the Runner control plane sits outside every per-work envelope with its own bounded footprint (slot-bounded reported set, file-backed task-log buffers/outboxes, slot-bounded journal). Ship the systemd unit/slice assets in the repository deployment assets so production isolation is declared, not implied.
acceptanceCriteria: A work item whose processes exceed their memory envelope is reclaimed/killed alone: the Runner process and all sibling work items continue, and poll/report/heartbeat stay operational (runner vitest with a fake WorkExecutionLauncher driving scope-termination back to the work key).

Containment completes within a bounded time via escalation, frees the execution slot, and reports a terminal `resource-contained` result with envelope facts to the owner — never `runner-lost`, never an unknown interruption (runner vitest + SpecTests for the terminal reason).
Nested descendant processes of a contained work item are terminated with the direct processes (tree-kill coverage in launcher tests).
The in-process fallback is used when systemd is unavailable and is exercised by the default test path; production path selects `systemd-run --scope` with a sanitized per-work unit name.

Deployment assets ship `mohist-runner.service` (MemoryMax), `mohist-runtime.slice`, and `mohist-work.slice`/`mohist-work-<workKey>.scope` patterns with documented envelopes; docs state that non-systemd/container environments are isolation-advised.
Runner control-plane footprint bounds are asserted: reported set is slot-bounded and task-log buffers/outboxes remain file-backed under the existing caps.
`npm test -w packages/runner` and `npm run docs:check` pass; Pi runtime process placement (in-process vs child) is verified before finalizing the launcher mapping and documented in notes.
tasks.output: Runner changes: WorkExecutionLauncher seam (systemd-run default + in-process fallback), containment detection/escalation/slot-free/`resource-contained` reporting wired into the executor; Deployment assets: systemd service/slice/scope units with envelope documentation; tests with a fake launcher.
tasks.notes: Design Decision H. Rejected in-process policing (RSS watchdog) as enforcement — the incidents showed the Node process itself is the runaway; only an external control reclaims without taking the control plane down. Envelope is the blast-radius bound; deadlines from T-006 are the correctness bound. Migration plan step 5.

tasks.title: Recovery status surfaces: wire projections, Web, CLI, and issue attention
tasks.description: Add an `interruption` projection `{state: interrupted|recovering, reasonCode, interruptedAt, recoveryDeadlineAt, nextAction}` to server wire task/status views, derived from the run's interruption record and the AgentJob ledger fields, with run status staying Running while nonterminal and `WorkflowStatusMapper` deriving presentation the same way it derives `blocked`. Render the states on every surface: Web workflow/run views show the interrupted task with its reason and deadline; CLI `mo run`/`mo runner` render `recovering`/`interrupted` with reason codes distinguishable from failed and from blocked unknown settlements; issue attention/inbox projections surface the interruption with its actionable reason. Sweep consumers of the breaking change: no surface may render these states as `runner-lost` failure or a context-free `session.abort fetch failed`; `resource-contained` and `runtime-unavailable`-style deferral diagnostics join the stable reason-code list.
acceptanceCriteria: Wire task/status views expose the interruption projection with state, reasonCode, interruptedAt, recoveryDeadlineAt, nextAction; run status stays Running while nonterminal (server SpecTests/UnitTests for projection derivation, including deadline-expired and resolved cases).

Web workflow run view presents a recoverable-interrupted task as interrupted with its recorded reason and deadline, never as a `runner-lost` terminal failure, and distinguishes it from a blocked unknown settlement (web tests).
`mo run`/`mo runner` output shows a recovering AgentJob as `recovering` with its reason code, distinguishable from a failed job and from blocked unknown settlements (CLI tests in Mohist.Cli.Tests).
Issue attention/inbox projection surfaces the interruption with its actionable reason and never a context-free failure (SpecTests for the projection).

Breaking sweep: grep confirms no consumer surface renders terminal `runner-lost` or unannotated `session.abort fetch failed` for active work; consumers keyed on `runner-lost` switch to the interruption/reason vocabulary.
`resource-contained` and deferral reason codes render with actionable wording on the surfaces.
`npm run test:fast` (incl. web, cli, runner suites) and `npm run typecheck:fast` pass.
tasks.output: Server wire interruption projections + WorkflowStatusMapper derivation; Web workflow/run view rendering; CLI `mo run`/`mo runner` rendering; issue attention/inbox projection; breaking-consumer sweep across surfaces; tests in all affected suites.
tasks.notes: Design Decision I. Reason-code strings are finalized here with the status-surface work (see design open questions: recovery-expired wording must read 'no Runner returned', not an execution verdict). Migration plan step 6.

tasks.title: End-to-end recovery verification and coordinated-release review
tasks.description: Verify the composed change end to end: process-restart recovery scenarios (OOM kill with in-flight and awaiting-ack work, reconnect with held work, late reports from a previous generation, deadline expiry) driven against the Runner host with fakes in the style of `execution-envelope.startup.test.ts`, plus the server-side closeout→redelivery→report→fallback lifecycle across the SpecTests. Review the coordinated-release ordering (Server first — old Runner poll bodies lack `readyRuntimes` and absence degrades to today's claim behavior — then Runners with the systemd slice assets, then Web/CLI), the rollback notes (SQLite backup before deployment; journal files are forward-only artifacts an older Runner ignores), and confirm the breaking-change sweep is complete.
acceptanceCriteria: End-to-end restart scenario tests exist and pass: Runner killed mid-execution with an awaiting-ack verdict and an executing work, restarted, first poll declares facts, verdict-backed work reports without re-execution, verdict-less work re-executes under the original identity, and each owner observes at most one outcome per identity.
Late-report and duplicate-report scenarios from a previous Runner generation reconcile idempotently across the composed server+runner tests.
Deadline-expiry scenario produces the named terminal fallback on both workflow work and AgentJobs; recovery-before-deadline produces none.
Two-fences invariant holds: no task ever carries both an AgentResultSettlement and a WorkInterruption (pinned by a cross-cutting test or assertion in the closeout tests).
Full `npm run verify` gate passes (docs:check, check:filesizes, format:check, build, all tests) with fake time and faked externals.
Release/rollback notes updated: deploy order Server→Runner→Web/CLI, backup requirement once new-state writes exist, journal forward-only behavior documented.
No terminal `runner-lost` presentation or untracked report dead end remains anywhere in server, runner, web, or CLI (grep-verified).
tasks.output: End-to-end restart/late-report/deadline scenario tests; verification report (verify gate green), release-ordering and rollback notes; final breaking-change sweep confirmation.
tasks.notes: Design Decision J (testability) and Migration plan step 7. Server tests use injected TimeProvider + Orleans reminder entry points; runner tests use RuntimeClock, file-system seam, fake WorkExecutionLauncher, vi.useFakeTimers.
